correctness.rationale: An invariant simplex is precisely a disjoint monomer/dimer packing on the cyclic set of antipodal columns, including the two distinct column dimers at n=2. Each dimer swaps two oriented simplicial vertices. The augmented alternating trace is minus the weighted packing partition function; summing freely over unused monomers cancels all non-spanning dimer packings, leaving two tilings only when n is even. Lefschetz and the precisely stated Agarwal–Basak published Betti ranks determine trace and order-two eigenmultiplicities. The exhaustive checker independently enumerated actual perfect matchings and all faces for n=2..9, and GF(2) exact chain ranks for n=2..8. These checks do not purport to prove the infinitely quantified statement, which has the cancellation proof.

originality.rationale: Main Theorem 1(b,c) in the directly inspected Agarwal–Basak arXiv:2608.30601v2 gives nonequivariant wedge ranks and degrees, which do not imply an involution action: there are inequivalent order-two actions with the same underlying vector-space ranks. Direct signed trace plus the order-two spectral constraint fills that gap. Targeted published-finding corpus and literature searches found no covering equivariant formula; no search-based certainty or independence is claimed.

value.rationale: The first recent all-parameter homotopy classification for this natural highly symmetric cubic graph family leaves its central involution representation genuinely undetermined. The result gives the complete rational C2 character for every ladder size (trivial even, balanced regular odd), a parity dichotomy not derivable from sphere counts alone. A structural monomer–dimer cancellation evaluates the character uniformly; its utility is symmetry-sensitive topology, not an arbitrary isolated numerical invariant. It does not claim a full dihedral or integral odd-case classification.
